business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Webtoon Publishing and Multilingual Chapter Unlocking

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Quebec private law follows the Civil Code of Quebec and the civilian tradition, while federal AML/CFT and criminal statutes operate within a common-law framework.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force October 1, 2014
Convention Between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital (1980), as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, S.O.R./2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part II.1 (money laundering and terrorist financing offences). Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 (beneficial-owner reporting and name authorization); An Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services, CQLR c D-9.2 (Quebec AML/CFT obligations for regulated financial intermediaries); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11 (name and commercial-document language rules).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the certificate of incorporation, articles, or constitutive deed of each corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations Canada or the relevant provincial corporate registry in the partner's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance for each corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation, including Registraire des entreprises du Québec for Quebec corporations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and proof of residential address of each general partner and each individual beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the limited partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or lawyer authorized in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Quebec resident agent or Quebec counsel for pre-incorporation filings and service acceptance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each general partner or duly authorized signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds / source-of-wealth declaration covering initial capital contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, legal, or accounting firm in the jurisdiction where the funds originate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization required only for documents originating in non-Hague states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of every general partner and every individual beneficial owner against the Consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions list, Canada's Special Economic Measures Act regulations, Canada's Autonomous Sanctions List issued by Global Affairs Canada, OFAC's SDN List, and applicable provincial securities commission cease-trade lists. PEP status is identified through licensed screening databases plus enhanced due diligence on source of wealth and source of funds for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates. All screening is conducted in accordance with FINTRAC compliance obligations under the PCMLTFA, with time-stamped results retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registre des entreprises du Québec, accessible online through the Services Québec portal (registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, every registered name of a Quebec legal person must have a French version. A name in another language may be used only as a secondary or complementary version, provided the French version is filed first and appears with at least equal prominence in commercial documents and signage. Non-Latin scripts are transliterated into Latin characters accepted by REQ; the French corporate designation for a Quebec limited partnership is 'société en commandite' and may be abbreviated as 'S.E.C.'
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: ROYAL / CROWN / QUÉBEC / CANADA / GOVERNMENT / MUNICIPAL
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation cannot be extended administratively; if the proposed limited partnership is not registered before the 30-day window expires, a new name request must be filed. Upon rejection, the applicant may, within 30 days of receipt of the REQ refusal notice, file a written administrative review request with Registraire des entreprises du Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, together with legal submissions and any corrected evidence. If the administrative review confirms the refusal, judicial review may be brought before the Superior Court of Quebec; counsel should be instructed promptly because the court challenge period is short.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this digital webtoon publishing file. Quebec law requires a genuine and accessible service address within Quebec for receipt of legal process and official communications; a registered agent's office or a virtual-office arrangement with a physical street address and consent for service will be accepted by REQ. No physical storefront or studio is required because the commercial activity consists of digital webtoon publication, multilingual chapter unlocking, and in-app payments through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated annualized probability below 5% absent a tax, AML, or commercial-substance audit trigger. REQ and Canadian tax authorities ordinarily use documentary review and written requests; unannounced physical inspection occurs only when a virtual office is demonstrably non-genuine or when a regulated activity is suspected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, Book Five (arts. 2186–2279), particularly arts. 2230–2236 on the société en commandite (limited partnership), supplemented by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c P-44.1), ss. 3, 7–25, and the Regulation respecting the application of that Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar) — Legal Publicity Branch
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; capital contributions are contractual and fixed in the limited partnership agreement. No escrow or paid-up capital deposit is required for registration, although Revenu Québec may, in exceptional non-resident cases, require a security deposit before granting a QST/GST account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the limited partnership has been constituted pursuant to the Québec Civil Code; RESOLVED: (1) the Limited Partnership Agreement is adopted and the subscribed capital contributions are confirmed in the amounts and instalments listed in the contribution schedule; (2) the registered office is fixed at the registered address in Québec, and statutory registers will be maintained accessible to all partners at that address; (3) the initial officers — managing partner, secretary, and compliance officer — are appointed, authorized jointly to open bank accounts and execute contracts, and severally to file declarations with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to instruct external counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification and optional name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name search and reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Launch a pre-clearance search in the REQ public register for the proposed partnership name, verifying that it is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing names. If the name contains a protected term or must be secured pending document preparation, file a name reservation request (demande de réservation de nom) via the REQ secure transaction service, pay the reservation fee, and obtain a name reservation certificate valid for 90 days. For a limited partnership, the corporate designation should include 'L.P.' or 's.e.c.' (société en commandite) if registered in French.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and name search report
Identity and domicile of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar rejects the name for confusion, prohibited terms, or misleading elements, file an amended reservation with a revised distinctive element; a refusal may be contested by a written review request to the REQ (review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises) or by judicial recourse before the Superior Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement and capital subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners and, where applicable, a notary of the Ordre des notaires du Québec for notarial deeds involving real property
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a written limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) specifying the partnership name, declared object, registered office address, identities and contributions of general and limited partners, the limitation of liability of limited partners, profit and loss allocation, management powers, admission and withdrawal rules, and dissolution triggers. Each partner executes the agreement; contributions may be made in cash, property, or industry, with cash contributions either deposited to a dedicated LP bank account or evidenced by an instalment schedule. If a partner contributes immovable property, the deed must be notarially executed to permit registration against the Quebec land register.
required_dossiers: Draft and executed limited partnership agreement
Capital contribution schedule or bank deposit receipt
Notarial deed if real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ flags missing mandatory clauses or contradictory partner information, the partners may execute an amending agreement (avenant) and file a corrected declaration of registration, which cures the defect retroactively provided no prejudiced third-party rights have accrued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration (déclaration d'immatriculation) with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online Mon Registre / secure transaction for the registration of a société en commandite
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration of the limited partnership through the REQ's secure e-filing service. Complete all mandatory fields: partnership name, establishment date, registered office in Québec, mailing address, general nature of the activity (NAICS 511130 digital publishing), the full names and addresses of all general partners, and the designated attorney in Québec if the partnership is not managed by a Québec-resident partner. Pay the applicable registration fee by card or pre-authorized debit. Upon acceptance, REQ issues an attestation d'immatriculation and assigns the Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ), which constitutes the conclusive legal publicity vesting the partnership.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Registration — limited partnership (REQ electronic form)
Executed copy of the partnership agreement
Proof of legal address and registered office in Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of non-receivability or demands rectification of the declaration, the partnership may file a modified declaration (déclaration modificative) within the delay indicated in the notice; a refusal to publicly register may be reviewed on request and, failing that, appealed to the Superior Court of Québec within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of tax accounts with Revenu Québec and the CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — Mon Dossier d'entreprise; Canada Revenue Agency — Business Registration (RC1 / intergovernmental confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the NEQ is assigned, register for the GST/HST (TPS/TVH) and QST (TVQ) accounts through the 'Registrations and updates' transaction in Mon Dossier d'entreprise. Revenu Québec synchronizes the creation of the federal business number and RT accounts with the CRA under the federal-provincial integration. Declare the principal business activity as digital webtoon publishing and chapter unlocking (NAICS 511130), indicate expected taxable supplies, and elect a fiscal year end. Where a payroll is anticipated, simultaneously subscribe the source deductions (employee CP/QPP, EI, income tax) account with Revenu Québec, which acts as the single-window administrator under the harmonized collection agreement.
required_dossiers: REQ attestation of registration and NEQ
Principal activity description and NAICS code
Expected turnover and taxable supplies estimate
Authorized officer contact details and identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA and Revenu Québec accounts are not synchronized within 15 days, file Form RC1 with the CRA for the business number and Form LM-1/V accompanying the QST registration request with Revenu Québec; a clearance or registration can be expedited by written request addressed to the tax services office, with an objection available within 90 days in case of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal occupancy permit and workplace compliance (if a physical office is established)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Québec municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal — Permits and Inspections Division); Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the partnership leases an office in Québec, apply for the municipal business licence or occupancy permit (permis d'exploitation or certificat d'occupation), attaching the lease, proof of conforming zoning, and building plans if alterations are made. Obtain a fire safety attestation from the local fire safety service for the premises. If employees are hired in Québec, register as an employer with the CNESST, obtain the employer promotion file, and compute the annual health and safety contribution; post the mandatory workplace notices and, where required, establish a health and safety committee.
required_dossiers: CNESST employer registration data and employee declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the permit on zoning grounds, submit a request for a minor derogation (dérogation mineure) to the municipal planning committee or apply for a change of use certificate; a CNESST classification may be reconsidered by filing an Application for Review within 60 days of the statement of classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — digital webtoon publishing and chapter-unlocking services are non-industrial activities; no manufacturing or industrial licensing board is engaged at the formation stage. If physical printing were later operated, the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) would become the relevant authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — no statutory operating licence is required for webtoon/digital comics syndication; only a standard municipal business permit (permis d'exploitation) and, for any brick-and-mortar office, an occupancy certificate apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction générale de l'analyse environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity consists exclusively of IP syndication, digital content licensing, and server/IT operations; no industrial establishment is created, so no full EIA or registration under the Environmental Quality Act (RLRQ c Q-2) is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at the registered-office scale: any office wastewater must comply with municipal sewer bylaws, residual materials (used electronics, toners, paper) must be managed under the Québec Residual Materials Regulation (RLRQ c E-30, r. 2) with recycling and hazardous waste sorting, and no VOC or atmospheric emission thresholds are engaged by IT-only operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety attestation under the Act respecting fire safety (RLRQ c S-3.4) for leased commercial premises; a municipal building/occupancy certificate confirming structural capacity and emergency access; and, where staff are employed, CNESST employer registration, the workplace health and safety clearance, and compliance with the Act respecting occupational health and safety (RLRQ c S-2.1), including the posting of emergency evacuation plans and first-aid equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax registration; Revenu Québec for Quebec QST registration, provincial income tax, and enterprise number (NEQ) via Registraire des entreprises. Portals: CRA My Business Account and Revenu Québec's online services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA and, for Quebec nexus, register with Registraire des entreprises to obtain the NEQ. If taxable supplies are made in Canada/Quebec and registration threshold is met, the partnership must open a GST/HST account and a QST account. The LP must provide partnership declaration details, identify the general partner/agent in Canada, and use the BN/NEQ for all filings. For foreign entities without Canadian establishment, simplified non-resident registration for GST/HST/QST can be completed online.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election analogous to the US. The LP is a fiscally transparent partnership for Canadian federal and Quebec income tax; no entity-level tax is imposed. Partners report their allocable shares. Tax elections available include deemed taxable Canadian business establishment elections, partnership fiscal-period elections, and QST/GST joint registration elections. Hybrid mismatch rules under Part XII of the Income Tax Act may require adjustments for foreign hybrid entities, but do not permit elective classification of a Quebec LP as a corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies worldwide or in Canada for GST/HST; CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Quebec for QST registration, with special rules for non-resident digital-services suppliers. A non-resident making supplies through a Canadian platform or carrying on business in Canada may be required to register regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or mandatory digital stamping regime currently applies to digital webtoon syndication. CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices. Businesses must maintain readable electronic records, and Quebec's evolving invoicing/electronic data exchange requirements do not currently impose API-based clearance for low-risk digital sellers. Third-party platform reporting rules apply separately to marketplace facilitators.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available on supplies of digital webtoon content (classified as intangible personal property) made to non-residents of Canada if the supply is not performed in, or consumed/used in, Canada. Subscriptions unlocked via Apple IAP or Google Play Billing are zero-rated for GST/HST/QST where the recipient is outside Canada and the contract for digital syndication is delivered offshore. Physical exports of printed materials are zero-rated only when genuine export occurs and the supplier retains documentary proof of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or electronic export reporting for physical media shipments
Commercial invoice and contract evidencing offshore recipient and passage of ownership
Bill of Lading / air waybill proving physical export from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank SWIFT confirmations, or payment settlement records from Apple/Google
Subscriber territorial data and platform payout reports showing non-resident download or unlock geography
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating where export documentation is incomplete. False statements or fraudulent claims can trigger reassessment, GST/HST civil penalties equal to 20% of net tax deficiency for false property basis, penalties up to 50% of the benefit sought, tax evasion criminal prosecution, interest charges, and retrospective QST/GST clawback plus fines. For digital export claims, CRA audits pay particular attention to IP location, platform user residency, and Apple/Google payout jurisdictions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with the Department of Finance Canada exercising ultimate foreign exchange policy responsibility and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions providing prudential supervision of authorized foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There is no exchange-control authority approval for profit remittances, dividends, interest, royalties, or partnership distributions. The practical hurdles are tax-related: non-resident partners of a Quebec Limited Partnership receiving distributions may be subject to Canadian Part XIII withholding or deemed Part XIII withholding, reduced by treaty eligibility; FATCA and CRS reporting obligations apply; FINTRAC large-transaction reporting applies; and the substance of any non-resident partner must be documented. Quebec provincial law does not impose currency conversion restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation deadline, or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. A Quebec LP engaged in webtoon publishing may retain foreign currency proceeds in its Canadian or offshore operating accounts. Goods-based export declarations under the Customs Act are not applicable to digital content export. The only low-friction obligations are FINTRAC record-keeping and the CAD 10,000 threshold report for large international electronic funds transfers.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Conditional Medium. Offshore digital electronic money institutions are not recognized as deposit-taking institutions in Canada and cannot open a domestic transactional account for a Quebec LP. They may only operate as a payment collection or disbursement gateway when engaging through a FINTRAC-registered Money Services Business or a payment service provider registered under the Retail Payment Activities Act. Direct routing of webtoon subscription revenue from Apple IAP or Google Play Billing to an offshore EMI wallet, without a Canadian-registered intermediary, poses regulatory concern and will be rejected by Canadian banks as open-loop payment activity; the safer model is EMI-to-bank settlement through a licensed Canadian PSP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act does not mandate universal physical attendance for corporate onboarding. In practice, Canadian Schedule I banks permit remote video identity verification for low-risk entities, but the Limited Partnership's general partner or a Quebec-resident authorized signatory is normally required to join an interactive KYC interview call. A fully remote account opening is feasible when the LP has no non-resident general partner and the ultimate beneficial owners pass enhanced due diligence; however, banks with a strict onboarding policy will require at least one physical in-branch confirmation of the signatory if a foreign RTIN or passport is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident LP partners and opaque beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organizational chart, certified LP agreement with partner schedule, passport and proof of address of every partner holding 25% or more, source of wealth statement for each substantial contributor, sanctions and adverse-media screening report, and a sworn statutory declaration confirming the true beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-service entity with nil Quebec operating footprint, creating conduit-risk inference
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec certificate, Quebec registered head office address with lease or serviced-office agreement, management resolution establishing the treasury function, ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130 business plan, and operational contracts with cloud content platforms and syndication licensees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue is almost entirely derived from app-store recurring billing, creating ambiguity about the underlying service
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple and Google merchant agreements, monthly settlement statements, webtoon copyright registrations or chain-of-title documents, list of unlocking and subscription SKU IDs, refund and chargeback history, and a ledger reconciling app-store settlement batches with the LP's GAAP revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through tax classification of the LP may suggest treaty shopping or tax-avoidance structuring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec tax counsel opinion confirming commercial non-tax-avoidance purpose, outline of planned Part XIII withholding for non-resident partners, Canada Revenue Agency trusts and partnerships correspondence, treaty residence certificates for all foreign partners, and the partnership information return evidencing ongoing Canadian business activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Incoming partner capital and licensing proceeds should be routed by SWIFT MT103 to the LP's benefitted bank account using the exact legal name of the Quebec LP, its Canadian BIC and transit number, and an unambiguous remittance message identifying the transaction as a partnership capital contribution, royalty, or revenue share. No fixed Statistics Canada purpose code is mandatory, but banks standardly record Investment or Royalty in field 70. For every wire equal to or above CAD 10,000, FINTRAC reporting is transmitted without suspending clearing; for larger partner injections the onboarding bank will request executed LP agreements, capital account statements, identity verification of contributing partners, and where treaty exemptions are claimed, form W-8BEN or NR601 certificates before crediting the account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements to licensors, creators, and international settling agents should be cleared through Payments Canada for domestic CAD payments, and through SWIFT MT103 with GPI tracking for foreign currency settlements. Commercial letters of credit are not appropriate for royalty, licensing, and licensing-disbursement streams because these are intangible services; a standby letter of credit may be issued only as a payment performance guarantee when a foreign syndication platform insists upon it. For low-value recurring payments to global creators, the treasury may use a registered MSB/PSP batch settlement rail that compresses individual creator remittances into a single MT103 settlement, preserving compliance with FINTRAC and Quebec data transfer rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter foreign exchange forward contracts under an ISDA Master Agreement or bank-form master with Schedule I Canadian banks
Foreign exchange swaps for CAD versus USD/EUR/GBP covering treasury cashflow mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps where the LP enters debt facilities denominated in foreign currency
Plain vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars on subscription revenue hedges
Non-deliverable forwards for illiquid webtoon-market currencies, settled in CAD at the Bank of Canada reference rate when no deliverable local currency market exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Declaration annuelle) for the limited partnership in the enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of the LP's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; the date stated in the registraire's reminder notice governs if different.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual declaration is not filed, the Registraire may issue a notice of default and, if the default remains unremedied, administratively cancel the registration; false or deficient declarations may attract fines up to CAD 10,000 under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 following the calendar year in which the limited partnership's fiscal period ended; T5013 slips to partners are due by the last business day of February.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a CRA penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500; continued default may lead to a compelled filing by the designated partner and associated compliance enforcement, but does not trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RL-15 / Releve 15 partnership information return for Quebec provincial tax purposes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of February following the calendar year in which the limited partnership's fiscal period ended.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500 under the Tax Administration Act; no strike-off applies, but the general partner may be assessed and partner tax attributes may be denied until the filing is made.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on a private Quebec limited partnership solely because of its legal form. A mandatory audit arises only if the limited partnership agreement or the unanimous agreement of partners requires it, or if the LP is a reporting issuer, a regulated financial institution, or holds a concession requiring audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under the CPA Canada Handbook; IFRS (Part I) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises, while a private limited partnership may elect Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II). IFRS is also required if the partnership agreement or a lender mandates it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must annually reconcile the Register of Limited Partners as at fiscal year-end, confirm each limited partnership unit transfer, update contribution schedules, and verify partner residency status, including non-residents for Income Tax Act purposes. Any change affecting the Quebec enterprise register must be filed as an amendment declaration within 30 days; the annual confirmation must be signed by the general partner, placed in the minute book, and retained with the statutory records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register of Limited Partners) - names, addresses, contributions, and unit transfer history
Register of Directors (Register of General Partners and managing representatives)
Minute Book - partnership resolutions, annual confirmations, and capital decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250-700 per year for a Quebec registered office or enterprise agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if no audit is required; USD 6,000-18,000 for a voluntary full audit of a small digital-publishing LP if mandated by the partnership agreement or a lender

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal + Quebec general corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); 12.2% combined reduced rate for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%). The Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent: the LP files information returns only; each partner reports allocated income at its own corporate/individual rate, and the corporate general partner becomes the taxable entity for operations conducted through the LP.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Fed SR&ED ITC: 35% refundable for CCPCs on first CAD 3M of qualified expenditures, otherwise 15% non-refundable. Quebec SR&ED credit: 30% refundable for SMEs, 14% for large corporations. Quebec interactive digital media (multimedia) refundable tax credit: up to 30% of eligible labour expenditures, subject to SODEC cultural recognition for the webtoon production. Provincial small business deduction and federal manufacturing/processing? no. Non-capital losses: carry back 3 years / forward 20 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 Statement of Partnership Income slips; filed via CRA My Business Account / Represent a Client portal (EFILE, XML Internet File Transfer). Quebec: TP-600 Series Partnership Information Return with partner RL slips; filed via Revenu Québec's Mon dossier d'entreprise portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013/TP-600 due within 5 months after the LP's fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end). Partner slips (T5013/RL) must be furnished to partners by the last day of February following the calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership Business Number (BN) assigned by CRA upon registration of the Quebec LP (15-character identifier).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned LPs must obtain a BN via CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1 before filing; a Canadian resident agent must be designated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident partner's share of business income (loss) from webtoon publishing for the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amount is taxable in Canada under Part I as income from carrying on business in Canada; no Part XIII withholding applies to the allocation itself, but the non-resident partner must file Canadian T1/T2 returns and pay instalments. Treaty protection must be claimed on the return, not at the partnership level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year-end date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the LP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the elected fiscal period; a non-calendar year-end requires CRA approval where the LP is controlled by non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Limited partner indicator (Y/N) and partner type code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identifying the partner as a limited partner activates at-risk rules: losses are deductible only to the extent of the partner's at-risk amount; non-resident limited partners face restrictions on deducting losses against other Canadian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of capital gains (losses) on dispositions of capital property, including IP portfolios.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gains on taxable Canadian property must be reported by the non-resident partner; treaty-protected gains require supporting waiver/analysis to be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of limited partnership loss for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Restricted by at-risk and limited-partner loss rules; excess losses may be carried forward and applied only against income from the same LP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of foreign source income and foreign taxes paid (e.g., global webtoon sublicensing royalties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claimed by each partner; non-resident partners combine this with Canadian-source allocations only for Canadian tax filing to determine foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner identification: full name, address, tax account (SIN/BN), and residence for tax purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must disclose country of residence, foreign tax identification number (TIN), and the treaty relied upon; disclosure supports treaty relief and reduced withholding application.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: minimum penalty of CAD 100 plus CAD 25 per partner per day of delinquency, capped at 100 days. Repeated failure or gross negligence adds penalties under s. 162/163 I.T.A. of up to 50% of misreported amounts and Quebec parallel penalties under the Tax Administration Act; interest accrues daily on all unpaid amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII federal withholding tax (s. 212(2) I.T.A.) on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation (e.g., a corporate general partner) to non-resident shareholders. Quebec imposes no additional dividend withholding tax. LP allocations of profit to non-resident partners are not dividends and are not subject to Part XIII withholding; instead, the non-resident partner is taxable under Part I on its allocated share of Canadian-source business income of the Quebec LP (and under Quebec's Taxation Act, subject to treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Protocol to claim reduced rates: (1) Obtain a tax residency certificate (TRC) from the partner's/beneficial owner's tax authority (US: IRS Form 6166; other jurisdictions: equivalent TRC including name, country, article of treaty, and fiscal year); (2) file CRA Form NR301 — Application for Certificate of Reduced Rate of Non-Resident Tax Withholding — with the TRC before the payment date; (3) present the approved certificate to the Canadian payer (or LP) to withhold at the treaty rate; (4) if excess tax was withheld, file Form NR7-R (Application for Refund of Part XIII Tax Withheld) within two years after the end of the calendar year; Quebec follows the federal determination for treaty-based reductions on dividends/royalties/interest and operates a parallel certificate process for withholding on payments to non-residents for services rendered in Quebec.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: 25% on IP royalties and 25% on interest (arm's-length interest exemption under s. 212(1)(b)(vii) eliminates withholding where the payee is unrelated and the debt is not participating). Canada–US treaty: 0% on copyright royalties of literary/artistic works (webtoon content and software licenses qualifying as such), 10% on patent/know-how royalties, 15% on participating-debt interest, and 0% on ordinary interest; non-treaty jurisdictions remain at 25%. Quebec: no separate provincial WHT on royalties/interest, but the income remains taxable to the non-resident under the Taxation Act.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 reporting threshold: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate fair market value of reportable non-arm's-length cross-border transactions in the taxation year. Country-by-Country Report threshold: CAD 1,000,000,000 (approx. EUR 750,000,000) consolidated group revenue. Contemporaneous OECD-aligned Local File/Master File documentation is not separately filed in Canada but must be prepared and furnished to the CRA on demand for any entity above the CAD 1M transaction threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations. Substance is enforced through: (i) the federal General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245 I.T.A.) and the Quebec anti-avoidance rule; (ii) the requirement that non-resident partners are taxable in Canada only if the LP 'carries on business' in Canada through a permanent establishment; (iii) Quebec extra-provincial registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; and (iv) GAAR's 'bona fide business purpose' and 'economic substance' tests. The Quebec LP must maintain substantial commercial activity in Quebec (employees, premises, server/logistics decisions, board-level management) to preserve its pass-through status, treaty access, and limited-liability shield.
